evidence: Defining behaviour is graded directly: 43 functional criteria cover typing/caret/multi-caret/undo/find/format/coloring, Run output, HTML preview, errors with line numbers, Stop/time-limit/supersede and isolation (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 24-330), and the save/conflict/history/live-library flows (lines 339-405). Durability is proven at two levels with real operations and readbacks, not health or static JSON: (1) the constraints gate cw_shared_saved_record (gates/constraints/judge.toml lines 27-33, aggregation all_pass, gate weight 0.0 in scoring.toml) saves through the UI, then clears localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, OPFS, service workers and cookies (app_context.md storage note) and reloads twice, so a browser-only store fails and the record must be server-backed; (2) scored cw_save_reload_restart (weight 1.5) uses the single-use restart_app tool, which test.sh's generated app-restart.sh implements as a real process-group kill and relaunch on the same DB_PATH, and then requires a fresh page to show the same record, current revision, history and each revision's exact source; the prompt forbids inferring a restart from a reload or health response. Shared server state across independent pages is separately exercised by cw_stale_save_refused (third-page fresh read), cw_history_restore_adds_revision (freshly loaded page), cw_restore_request_repeat_safe and cw_live_library_update (second tab/context). All of these trace to public requirements in behaviour.md and integration.md (survive reloads and complete process restarts; library shared between independent browser contexts). Counterexample attempts: a localStorage/IndexedDB-only app fails the gate; an in-memory server store passes the gate but fails cw_save_reload_restart after the real restart; a third-party hosted store (network is public) would legitimately be server-backed and survive restart, consistent with the workbook note that server-backed is not same-origin; a conforming app that refuses a replayed restore via base-revision check or a persisted operation id passes, so no hidden mechanism is required. Runtime: raw-evidence-index hashes all match; scripted golden restart.json shows 3 revisions (save, save, restore) intact after a real restart and persist-after.json cw_save_reload_restart true. Residual risk (why risk=true): no full configured-judge run exists on these v16 bytes (index scope says hosted runs are v15 only with different functional criteria), so whether the configured judge actually executes the clear-storage gate and the single-use restart correctly on v16 is unmeasured; scripted Playwright evidence is not judge evidence. Minor design note: SQLite itself cannot be proven by a browser judge (a JSON-file store would pass), which is a technology-mandate coverage question for another row, not a durability defect here.
run_verdict: PASS (static design + scripted golden); configured-judge run on v16 bytes NOT MEASURED
